mark_affecting.quote: It's literally eating the miles, reaching her apron and climbing right up her belt.

flagged.title: Form, Structure & Language
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly states that Blake's 'London' has 14 lines (it has 16), misidentifies Jennings's 'Absence' as tercets instead of quintains, and claims Alvi's poem has no stanza breaks at all.

mark_affecting.quote: Blake's poem London is also exactly 14 lines, but it's built out of quatrains instead. Many critics actually read it as a dark anti-sonnet

mark_affecting.video_says: Then we have Jennings using three-line tercets, a compressed form mirroring severe emotional restraint
mark_affecting.lesson_says: Jennings’s 'Absence' contracts into tight five-line stanzas / Quintains (5-line stanzas): Jennings ('Absence').

mark_affecting.video_says: And Alvi uses absolutely no stanza breaks at all, creating a continuous flow for a mind deep in unresolved thought.
mark_affecting.lesson_says: Alvi ('Presents from my Aunts in Pakistan') instead uses seven stanzas of very different lengths, which mirrors her unresolved thought process.
